CHEMISTRY — TERMLY EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.

8. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.

12. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

13. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

14. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.

   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.

----

18. In three clear sentences, explain Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
